subject: OrbitWise MAP: finalizing security acceptance & retention terms
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari.patel@orbitwise.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lee Park <lee.park@orbitwise.io>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood MAP / Security intake for OrbitWise evaluation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — OrbitWise is keen to move quickly on a short evaluation and we need to lock the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and clear security gates so procurement can start paperwork. To kick off: can you share a proposed MAP that lists acceptance gates (SOC 2, SIG/CAIQ, DPA finalization, retention windows), estimated timelines, and what evidence you can provide?

A few items from our side we care about up front:
- SOC 2: we need a recent Type II (redacted acceptable) and a summary of scope (data flows, any subservice orgs).
- SIG/CAIQ: completed questionnaire or a CAIQ export; we will review controls tied to key management and encryption at rest/in transit.
- DPA: can you confirm your baseline retention options and whether you support EU-only residency for keys/data?
- Evidence cadence: we have a procurement window the week of July 12 — can compliance sign-off land by then if we compress?

I attached our intake doc to capture answers. Suggest we put together a 3-week MAP but open to your suggestion if you have a standard path.

Appreciate quick turnaround — copying Lee (security) to loop in their technical checks.

Best,
Ari
Product Ops, OrbitWise

Attachment: OrbitWise-Security-Intake.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@orbitwise.io>
Cc: Lee Park <lee.park@orbitwise.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP / Security intake for OrbitWise evaluation

Hi Ari — great to hear. Thanks for the clear asks. I’m attaching a draft MAP (RW_MAP_v1.xlsx) and an initial list of evidence we can provide. High level proposal below; happy to tighten timelines to meet procurement.

Proposed condensed MAP (4 workstreams, 3 weeks—can compress to 2 weeks with parallel review):
1) Intake & scope (2 business days): finalize scope (models, data types, residency).
2) Controls evidence (3–5 business days): deliver redacted SOC 2 Type II, completed SIG/CAIQ export, KMS diagram, and encryption notes.
3) Technical validation (4–6 business days): test in staging (EU region option available), bake in prefix-caching limits and observability hooks for your telemetry team.
4) Legal & DPA (3–5 business days): exchange redlines, finalize DPA and retention annex.

What Redwood will provide now (attachments + notes):
- SOC2-redacted.pdf: latest Type II report covering infra and serving runtime (redacted vendor details OK).
- SIG-answers.xlsx: completed CAIQ export with control mappings (we’ll highlight KMS/egress controls).
- RW_MAP_v1.xlsx: MAP draft with acceptance criteria per gate and owners.
- KMS/network diagram (will send separately): shows key lifecycle, HSM/KMS provider and customer key options for private deployments.

Retention baseline options we recommend (we can include as DPA annex):
- Short (30 days): token-level logs only, retention for troubleshooting (default for hosted sandbox).
- Standard (90 days): logs + short-term request traces (recommended for evaluations).
- Extended (365 days): full request trace history (enterprise / audit requirements).

EU residency: we support EU-region hosting and can propose a cappable plan for EU-only data residency for evaluation (we’ll note caveats around third-party logging and backups in the MAP).

Next steps:
- I’ll post the MAP to the drive and send DocuSign stub for the DPA redline tomorrow.
- Grace — can you confirm whether we can provide the KMS diagram and a limited-scope SOC2 extract by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks — I’m available for a 30-min sync today if that helps accelerate.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: RW_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 22KB); SOC2-redacted.pdf (pdf, 540KB); SIG-answers.xlsx (xlsx, 110KB)

From: Lee Park <lee.park@orbitwise.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ari Patel <ari.patel@orbitwise.io>
Date: 2027-06-26T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP / Security intake for OrbitWise evaluation

Karthik / Grace — thanks for the quick reply and the draft MAP. A couple of clarifying questions from security so we can scope the SIG review and evidence collection: 

1) SIG scope: will the CAIQ include full control text for the serving runtime and orchestration plane, or is it limited to data plane controls? We need control-level answers for key management (KMS rotation, HSM use), identity (SAML/SCIM), and incident response.
2) SOC2 extract: is the report inclusive of subcontractors that provide GPU infra (we need to know where compute and backups live). Redacted is OK but please indicate vendor boundaries.
3) DPA / retention: for EU-only evaluation, we must see an affirmative data residency configuration and an annex that states no cross-border backups for the evaluation environment. Is that something you can commit to for a short-term POC?
4) Evidence format & timing: we can run SIG control review in parallel to a light SOC2 check, but procurement needs a signed DPA by July 12. Can Redwood provide a DPA redline this week and a target for final signoff?

If you can answer 1–3 inline and attach the KMS/network diagram and the SIG sheet, we’ll prioritize our review. If we compress to a two-week MAP, we’ll need the SOC excerpt + DPA redline by Friday (6/28).

Thanks — Lee
Security Lead, OrbitWise

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lee Park <lee.park@orbitwise.io>, Ari Patel <ari.patel@orbitwise.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP / Security intake for OrbitWise evaluation — answers & action items

Lee / Ari — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline and an actionable runbook to meet your July 12 procurement target (we’ll be pragmatic about scope for the POC).

SIG scope: the attached SIG-answers.xlsx is a full CAIQ export scoped to our inference product and orchestration layer. We’ve flagged control owners in column D and added notes for KMS, identity, and incident response. Short answers:
- KMS: we operate customer-key options (BYOK) via our KMS provider (HSM-backed) and offer a Redwood-managed default. Rotation policies and key lifecycle diagrams included in the KMS-network-diagram.png.
- Identity: we support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning; API keys for service-to-service with scoped roles.

SOC2 scope and vendors: SOC2-redacted.pdf is our most recent Type II covering our serving runtime and control environment. GPU infra is provided by a cloud partner; the report’s scoping appendix clearly marks the subservice boundaries (we’ve added a one-page extract in the MAP to make that explicit).

EU-only evaluation: we can spin up a dedicated evaluation staging in EU region that restricts compute and primary logs to EU region for a 30/90-day POC. Caveat: backups and certain monitoring alerts routed through vendor endpoints may require limited cross-border egress; we will enumerate exact endpoints in the MAP annex and offer compensating controls (encryption-in-transit, minimised metadata).

DPA and retention: we will send a DPA redline via DocuSign by EOD Friday (6/28). Proposed retention defaults for the POC: 90 days for request traces (recommended), 30 days for token-level ephemeral logs; extension to 365 days available as an enterprise add-on. We’ll include a retention annex to explicitly state EU residency for the evaluation environment.

Action items and owners (short runbook):
- Grace O'Connor: upload KMS-network-diagram.png and SOC2 extract to Drive (today EOD).
- Marissa Cole: prepare DPA redline and send DocuSign link (target EOD 6/28).
- Karthik Iyer: update RW_MAP_v1.xlsx with acceptance criteria and send HubSpot deal link.
- OrbitWise: confirm compressed two-week path or accept the 3-week MAP; confirm scope and list of test accounts for staging.

Attachments: SIG-answers.xlsx (xlsx, 160KB), KMS-network-diagram.png (png, 95KB)

If this plan looks good we’ll proceed and mark the DPA as the critical path for July 12 procurement. Happy to jump on a 20-min call this afternoon to close open questions.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success (Security liaison), Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

--
Marissa Cole
Legal Ops (cc'd for DPA)
marissa.cole@redwood.com
